title: GPU SlimMode: probe-reserve quiet-down and fail-safe model downgrade
creator: Ravi Shah
description: Introduce a lightweight runtime mode ("SlimMode") that dynamically reduces GPU working set by: 1) probing low-impact requests to detect imminent memory pressure (probe-reserve), 2) entering a short quiet-down period where non-critical batching/admission is throttled, and 3) invoking a deterministic fail-safe path that downgrades to a lower-memory model variant or subgraph (stitch-model) instead of triggering OOM. This ticket covers design, prototype, and integration with existing KV cache eviction signals and continuous batching admission controls.
motivation: Recent tail OOM incidents show that aggressive continuous batching combined with large KV footprints can push pods past the OOM cliff within the span of a single high-concurrency window. Existing reactive eviction causes high latency spikes and lost responses. SlimMode aims to create a short, deterministic escape hatch that avoids full OOMs and preserves useful responses by trading fidelity for survivability.
approach: Probe-reserve: schedule small synthetic probes (very low token / prefix) when scheduler detects accelerating GPU allocation growth; if probe allocation fails or memory watermark crosses threshold, reserve a small emergency allocation pool and mark node as 'soft-constrained'

Quiet-down: reduce admission rate for best-effort windows, shrink per-request KV reservations conservatively, and shorten batching windows for new requests for up to 500ms to relieve allocation pressure without dropping in-flight tokens

SlimMode model downgrade (stitch-model): for requests flagged as non-strict (per route/policy) route to a pinned lower-memory variant or execute a slice of the original model (e.g., skip high-attention layers / run with lower precision per-layer) with a structured annotation in the response explaining the degraded mode

Deterministic retry/upgrade: automated background task attempts to rehydrate KV reservations and, if the node returns to safe memory levels within 1s-3s, transparently retry the downgraded requests (if idempotent) or mark for partial-response completion according to route policy
Metrics + tracing: emit granular events for probe outcomes, quiet-down windows, downgrade activations, and retries to feed Console and alerting rules
acceptance_criteria: Under synthetic high-concurrency KV-heavy tests, pods that would previously OOM remain alive and return either full or documented downgraded responses
End-to-end latency p95 for critical routes increases by no more than 15% during SlimMode windows versus baseline
Console shows probe/reserve/quiet-down events and provides a per-route breakdown of downgraded responses with counts and sample traces
Automated canary confirms transparent retry path for idempotent requests: at least 95% successful recovery within 3 retries in synthetic scenarios
Feature toggles exist (per-deployment and per-route) to opt in/out and to adjust thresholds for probe and quiet-down
technical_notes: Memory watermark detection will use a composite signal: GPU alloc growth rate (short window), KV committed entries, and recent unsuccessful batch admissions
Probe requests are instrumented mini-requests with highest priority thin-path; they must never evict user KV entries and should be capped to a single micro-batch

SlimMode downgrades implemented as model adapter layer that can: switch to a quantized variant, reduce attention passes for long-context requests, or run a distilled head produced by model onboarding pipeline

KV conservative trimming: instead of full eviction, mark cold prefixes as 'eviction-candidates' and allow background compaction to reclaim space; during quiet-down, admission will prefer requests that hit hot KV entries
We will reuse existing rollout/feature-flag infra for per-customer thresholds and allow ops to trigger emergency off switch
Safety: never downgrade requests annotated with 'strict' in route metadata (e.g., legal transcripts); these will instead be rejected with structured backoff responses
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Downgraded responses might be unacceptable for certain customers — Mitigation: per-route strictness, explicit response meta explaining downgrade and opt-in config
Risk: Probe-reserve overhead could increase load — Mitigation: probes are extremely small, frequency limited and disabled when cluster load is normal
Risk: Complex interactions with autoscaler leading to thrashing — Mitigation: introduce hysteresis windows and do not change cluster scaling decisions solely based on probe signals
Risk: Model adapter correctness — Mitigation: add unit tests for stitch-model paths and run canary traffic against a subset of hosts before wider rollout
qa_plan: Create synthetic workload harness with bursty prefix distributions and large KV footprints (link to job below)
Two canaries: internal staging (100qps) and high-load canary (1k concurrent) to observe Slack alerts and Console traces
Chaos test: simulate a slow background compaction to force repeated quiet-down windows and verify stability
Regression checks: ensure existing eviction metrics and billing traces are unchanged for non-SlimMode traffic
